LESSON: THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.2: Thoughts and feelings

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Thoughts and feelings. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: why it is good to be joyful, 1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify good thoughts and feelings,
2. explain the importance of being joyful,
3. list lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26, The learner is guided to: thoughts and feelings, sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful, respecting others, control your thoughts and feelings? with anger or sadness? Ϯ
4. apply the lessons learnt to cope with emotions in day-to-day life. cope with emotions such as anger or sadness, colour pictures of faces depicting various emotions, when wronged, down lessons learnt cards and recite it, in the Lord always (Philippians 4:4). 3

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify good thoughts and feelings,

2. explain the importance of being joyful,

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Thoughts and feelings.
2. Explain Thoughts and feelings to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: sing a song related to good thoughts and feelings,
4. Show that you can: identify good thoughts and feelings,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Thoughts and feelings. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: why it is good to be joyful, 1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Sing a song related to good thoughts and feelings,
2. List good thoughts such as sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful, respecting others,

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify good thoughts and feelings,
2. explain the importance of being joyful,
3. list lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26, The learner is guided to: thoughts and feelings, sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful, respecting others, control your thoughts and feelings? with anger or sadness? Ϯ
4. apply the lessons learnt to cope with emotions in day-to-day life. cope with emotions such as anger or sadness, colour pictures of faces depicting various emotions, when wronged, down lessons learnt cards and recite it, in the Lord always (Philippians 4:4). 3
